svg.title: Research interests: the logical architecture of the mind. Memory: why does working memory hold so little, and is its limit a fixed number of slots or a shared resource? The sketch plots precision against set size, a slot model with a kink at k items beside a smoothly declining resource model. Attention: how does attention allocate a limited capacity across competing inputs? One fixed capacity bar is split into one, two and four shares. Decision: how do decisions emerge from noisy evidence, and how can signal detection theory separate sensitivity from bias? Two overlapping noise and signal distributions with a criterion line. My background in Computer Science and Engineering gives me formal logic, probability, algorithms and code for simulation and statistical modelling.

section.h2: The questions that pull me in are about the mind's logical architecture.

div.p: Why does working memory hold so little, and is its limit a fixed number of slots or a shared resource?
How does attention allocate a limited capacity across competing inputs?
How do decisions emerge from noisy evidence, and how can signal detection theory separate sensitivity from bias?

section.p: Why I can do it: my background in Computer Science and Engineering gives me formal logic, probability, algorithms and code for simulation and statistical modelling.
